lessons.title: आणि (āṇi) — and
lessons.gloss: and — the one word that turns two Marathi sentences you can already say into one

segments.text: Say two sentences you already own: मला चहा आवडतो, and मला दूध आवडतं. Two sentences, two breaths. This chapter makes them one.
आणि — āṇi — and.
मला चहा आवडतो आणि दूध आवडतं. — malā chahā āvaḍto āṇi dūdh āvaḍtaṁ. — I like tea and I like milk.

आणि (āṇi) sits BETWEEN the two pieces and changes nothing on either side. Each half keeps its own agreement: चहा is masculine and keeps आवडतो, दूध is neuter and keeps आवडतं. The joining word does not reach inside.
It joins two nouns just as happily: भाऊ आणि (āṇi) बहीण, brother and sister.

The word is old and slightly surprising. It comes from Sanskrit अन्य (anya), "other." A word for the other one wore down into a word for one more. English does the same trick from the other side: another is an other.

segments.instruction: bhāū āṇi bahīṇ — brother and sister
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *bhāū āṇi bahīṇ* — brother and sister]

segments.instruction: malā chahā āvaḍto āṇi dūdh āvaḍtaṁ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *malā chahā āvaḍto āṇi dūdh āvaḍtaṁ*]

segments.source: [YOU SAY: which half of that sentence changed when you joined it — **neither**]

segments.prompt: Join brother and sister into one Marathi phrase.

feedback.incorrect: Put āṇi between them and change nothing else.

segments.text: Where does आणि (āṇi) sit, and what does it change? (Between the two pieces; nothing.) What did it originally mean? (Other.)
Sources: Wiktionary: आणि (āṇi).

lessons.title: किंवा (kiṁvā) — or
lessons.gloss: or — the word that offers a choice, and the word every multiple-choice question is built from

segments.text: One lesson ago you got आणि (āṇi), which adds. Say चहा आणि (āṇi) पाणी. Now you need the word that does the opposite: it puts two things side by side and asks you to take only one.
किंवा — kiṁvā — or.
चहा किंवा पाणी? — chahā kiṁvā pāṇī? — Tea or water?
It sits exactly where आणि (āṇi) sat. The two words are a matched pair: same slot, opposite job. आणि (āṇi) hands you both, किंवा (kiṁvā) makes you choose.

Taken apart, किंवा (kiṁvā) is two Sanskrit words carried over whole: किम् (kim), "what" — the same stem that gave Marathi काय — plus वा (vā), an ancient particle meaning "or." That वा is genuinely old: Latin kept it as the -ve in sīve, "or if." Marathi's word for choosing is, underneath, "what-or."

segments.instruction: the same pair with āṇi, and hear the offer become a list
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the same pair with *āṇi*, and hear the offer become a list]

segments.prompt: Offer a guest a choice between tea and milk, then offer them both.
acceptedResponses: chahā kiṁvā dūdh? — chahā āṇi dūdh
चहा किंवा दूध? चहा आणि दूध
chaha kinva dudh chaha ani dudh

feedback.incorrect: kiṁvā offers the choice; āṇi hands over both.

segments.text: Which of the two joining words makes the listener choose? (किंवा (kiṁvā).) What two Sanskrit words is it made of? (किम् + वा, "what or".)
Sources: Wiktionary: किंवा (kiṁvā).

lessons.title: पण (paṇ) — but
lessons.gloss: but — the word that lets a Marathi sentence take something back

segments.text: Two joining words are yours: आणि (āṇi) adds, किंवा (kiṁvā) offers. Say चहा आणि (āṇi) दूध, then चहा किंवा (kiṁvā) दूध. Both are friendly. Neither can disagree with anything.
पण — paṇ — but.
चहा आहे पण दूध नाही. — chahā āhe paṇ dūdh nāhī. — There is tea but there is no milk.

पण (paṇ) stands in the same slot as the other two and does the one thing they cannot: it lets the second half push back against the first. Until you have it, every sentence you can build only agrees with itself.

पण (paṇ) and पुन्हा — the again in पुन्हा भेटू — are the same Sanskrit word, पुनर् (punar), "again, back." One descendant kept the time meaning; the other kept only the back, and turned it into contradiction. English does this too: but began as be-utan, "outside."

segments.instruction: the three joining words in a row — āṇi, kiṁvā, paṇ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the three joining words in a row — *āṇi*, *kiṁvā*, *paṇ*]

segments.instruction: which Marathi word for again is पण (paṇ)'s twin — punhā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which Marathi word for *again* is **पण**'s twin — *punhā*]

segments.prompt: Fill the same slot three ways with chahā and dūdh: add, offer, contradict.
acceptedResponses: chahā āṇi dūdh; chahā kiṁvā dūdh; chahā āhe paṇ dūdh nāhī
चहा आणि दूध चहा किंवा दूध चहा आहे पण दूध नाही

feedback.incorrect: Same position each time: āṇi, kiṁvā, paṇ.

segments.text: Which joining word lets the second half disagree with the first? (पण (paṇ).) Which everyday farewell word is its twin? (पुन्हा.)
Sources: Wiktionary: पण (paṇ).

lessons.title: The same gap, three ways
lessons.gloss: one slot, three relations — add, offer, contradict

segments.text: Three words landed in this chapter and all three go in the same place. Name them in the order you met them.

segments.instruction: malā chahā āvaḍto āṇi dūdh āvaḍtaṁ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *malā chahā āvaḍto āṇi dūdh āvaḍtaṁ*]

segments.prompt: Say chahā and pāṇī joined three ways: added, offered as a choice, and contradicted.
acceptedResponses: chahā āṇi pāṇī; chahā kiṁvā pāṇī; chahā āhe paṇ pāṇī nāhī
चहा आणि पाणी चहा किंवा पाणी चहा आहे पण पाणी नाही

feedback.correct: Three relations out of one slot.
feedback.incorrect: Run them in order: āṇi, kiṁvā, paṇ.

segments.text: Which one hands over both? (आणि (āṇi).) Which one makes you pick? (किंवा (kiṁvā).) Which one takes something back? (पण (paṇ).) Then stop.
